## Minimal working answer

::: {.scrollable}

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Map the density of recorded fatal shootings in NYC in 2019,
# excluding Staten Island. Run in the crime_mapping workspace.

## Load packages and data ------------------------------------------------------

# Note: both datasets will be harmonised to use EPSG:6538 for use with
# `hotspot_kde()`

# Load packages
pacman::p_load(ggspatial, here, httr2, sf, sfhotspot, tidyverse)

# Download the original data into the workspace
request("https://mpjashby.github.io/crimemappingdata/nyc_shootings.csv") |>
  req_perform(path = here("data", "raw", "nyc_shootings.csv"))
request("https://mpjashby.github.io/crimemappingdata/nyc_precincts.gpkg") |>
  req_perform(path = here("data", "raw", "nyc_precincts.gpkg"))

# Read local shootings data and select fatal shootings in 2019
shootings <- read_csv(here("data", "raw", "nyc_shootings.csv")) |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  filter(murder == TRUE, boro != "STATEN ISLAND") |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = "EPSG:4326") |>
  st_transform("EPSG:6538")

# Load NYC police precincts data
precincts <- here("data", "raw", "nyc_precincts.gpkg") |>
  read_sf() |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  # Filter out precincts in Staten Island, since there are very few fatal
  # shootings there and it takes up a lot of space due to the position of Staten
  # Island relative to the rest of NYC
  filter(precinct <= 119) |>
  st_transform("EPSG:6538")


## Wrangle data ----------------------------------------------------------------

# Calculate KDE
shootings_kde <- shootings |>
  hotspot_kde(
    grid = hotspot_grid(precincts, cell_size = 250),
    bandwidth_adjust = 0.33,
    quiet = TRUE
  ) |>
  hotspot_clip(precincts, quiet = TRUE)


## Make map --------------------------------------------------------------------

shootings_map <- hotspot_map(
  shootings_kde,
  basemap_type = "cartolight",
  caption = str_glue(
    "Author: Joe Bloggs, Date produced: {lubridate::today()}\n",
    "Shootings: New York City Police Department\n",
    "Boundaries: City of New York (CC BY 3.0 AU)"
  )
) +
  geom_sf(data = precincts, colour = "grey33", fill = NA) +
  geom_sf_label(
    aes(label = scales::ordinal(precinct)),
    data = precincts,
    alpha = 0.5,
    colour = "grey33",
    fill = "white",
    size = 2.5,
    linewidth = NA
  ) +
  annotation_scale(width_hint = 1 / 5, style = "ticks", location = "br") +
  labs(
    title = str_glue(
      "Density of recorded fatal shootings in New York City"
    ),
    subtitle = str_glue(
      "Fatal shootings recorded by NYC Police, 2019, excluding Staten Island"
    ),
    fill = "density of\nshootings"
  ) +
  # Make the map square (i.e. have an aspect or height/width ratio of 1) to
  # expand the area covered by the map without reducing the size of the area
  # covered by the data layer
  fixed_plot_aspect(ratio = 1) +
  theme(
    # We're going to overlay the legend on the map, so we should give the
    # legend a solid background
    legend.background = element_rect(colour = NA, fill = "#F2F2F2"),
    # Use the top-right corner of the legend as the anchor point for determining
    # its position
    legend.justification = c(1, 1),
    # Make the legend colour bar smaller
    legend.key.width = unit(0.8, "lines"),
    # Create a margin around the legend, since it has a solid background
    legend.margin = margin(6, 6, 6, 6),
    # Move the top-right corner of the legend to be very near the top-right
    # corner of the map
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(0.98, 0.98),
    # Make the legend and title smaller to reduce their visual prominence
    legend.text = element_text(size = rel(0.7)),
    legend.title = element_text(size = rel(0.8)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = rel(0.8), margin = margin(3, 0, 6, 0)),
    plot.caption = element_text(colour = "grey45", size = rel(0.7), hjust = 0)
  )


# Save the finished map in the workspace output folder
ggsave(
  here("output", "nyc_fatal_shootings_2019.png"),
  plot = shootings_map,
  width = 210,
  height = 210,
  units = "mm"
)
```

## :warning: Read the instructions

## :angry: Not acting on last week's feedback

::: {.nobullets}
* Lines (**including comments**) over 80 characters long
* Comments that don't start with `#` _and a space_, e.g. `# This is a comment`

## :sunglasses: Non-misleading density estimates


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-line-numbers="3,7"}
shootings_kde <- shootings |>
  hotspot_kde(
    grid = hotspot_grid(precincts, cell_size = 400), #<1>
    bandwidth_adjust = 0.33,
    quiet = TRUE
  ) |>
  hotspot_clip(precincts) #<2>
```
:::

1. Provide a grid that covers the whole area you have data for
2. Clip the result to the area for which you have data

#### Option 3: only show some labels (advanced)

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-line-numbers="1-12,18"}
# Identify precincts with highest density of fatal shootings
high_density_precincts <- shootings_kde |>
  # Join precinct names to KDE grid cells based on location
  st_join(precincts) |>
  # Convert from SF object to tibble to make `count()` faster
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  # Count total density of fatal shootings in each precinct
  count(precinct, wt = kde) |>
  # Keep precincts with highest density of fatal shootings
  slice_max(order_by = n, n = 10) |>
  # Join precinct names back to boundaries of precincts for mapping
  left_join(precincts, by = join_by("precinct")) |>
  st_as_sf()

hotspot_map(shootings_kde) +
  geom_sf(data = precincts, colour = "grey33", fill = NA) +
  geom_sf_label(
    aes(label = scales::ordinal(precinct)),
    data = high_density_precincts,
    alpha = 0.5,
    colour = "grey33",
    fill = "white",
    label.size = NA
  )
```

## :no_entry_sign: Code that creates/overwrites unnecessary objects



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-line-numbers="2,5,9,12"}
# Load and wrangle fatal shootings in New York data
nyc_shootings <- read_csv(here::here("data", "raw", "nyc_shootings.csv"))

# Clean column names and convert to spatial data
nyc_shootings <- janitor::clean_names(nyc_shootings) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = "EPSG:4326")

# Transform fatal shootings data to a projected CRS (EPSG:6538)
nyc_shootings_projected <- st_transform(nyc_shootings, crs = "EPSG:6538")

# Filter only fatal shootings
fatal_shootings <- nyc_shootings_projected |>
  filter(murder == TRUE)
```
:::

## How to fix errors in your R code

[Checklist for handling code errors](https://books.lesscrime.info/learncrimemapping/appendices/handling_errors.html)

::: {.scrollable}

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Load packages
pacman::p_load(ggspatial, here, httr2, sf, sfhotspot, tidyverse)


# Load data --------------------------------------------------------------------

# Download data from the web and save to local file
request("https://mpjashby.github.io/crimemappingdata/nyc_shootings.csv") |>
  req_perform(path = here("data", "raw", "nyc_shootings.csv"))
request("https://mpjashby.github.io/crimemappingdata/nyc_precincts.gpkg") |>
  req_perform(path = here("data", "raw", "nyc_precincts.gpkg"))

# Load shootings data
shootings <- here("data", "raw", "nyc_shootings.csv") |>
  read_csv() |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = "EPSG:3246") |>
  filter(murder == TRUE) |>
  st_transform("EPSG:6538")

# Load NYC police precincts data
precincts <- here("data", "raw", "nyc_precincts.gpkg") |>
  read_sf() |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  filter(precinct < 120) |>
  st_transform("EPSG:6538")


## Wrangle data ----------------------------------------------------------------

# Calculate KDE
shootings_kde <- shootings |>
  hotspot_kde(
    grid = hotspot_grid(precincts, cell_size = 400),
    bandwidth_adjust = 0.33,
    quiet = TRUE
  ) |>
  hotspot_clip(precincts)


## Make map --------------------------------------------------------------------

hotspot_map(shootings_kde, basemap_type = "cartolight") +
  geom_sf(data = precincts, colour = "grey33", fill = NA) +
  geom_sf_label(
    aes(label = scales::ordinal(precinct)),
    data = precincts,
    alpha = 0.5,
    colour = "grey33",
    size = 2.25,
    label.size = NA
  ) +
  fixed_plot_aspect(ratio = 1)
```

  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current

  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);

    }

</script>
